stage1.impression: A moody, credible night set: the board-formed concrete with its tie holes and the red V of light thrown up both sides of the speaker are the best things in the frame, and the wet tiles carry a convincing reflection. But the speaker reads as a glowing red lightbox whose interior burns to pink-white, the horn above it is an almost black slab with a dark blob in it, the wall directly above the speaker gets no colour at all, and the plinth and the strip of floor under it read as a muddy dark band rather than a deliberate black object on wet stone.

blocking_9: Ember red reads as red, not pink-white, at the cabinet's brightest points: ports and lit batts below lum 200 with g and b medians well under r (now ports 246/237/237, lum 239)

The wall directly above and behind the speaker carries the speaker's colour (now r36 g28 b38 there, neutral), so the colour on the wall reads as a halo around the speaker, not two side wedges with a gap
The speaker stands a metre in front of the wall as the brief says (now its back is about 85 mm from the wall's face), so wall and speaker separate in depth
The plinth reads as a clean matte black object and the floor runs continuously from the wall foot into the wet tiles with no dark dry band or hard horizontal seam
The horn reads as tinted resin catching some light, not a black silhouette (needs bounce from a coloured wall; the horn itself is fixed)

defects.what: Right port interior clips to near-white (lum 239, rgb 246/237/237); left port the same at about [665,1160,725,1210]. Ember red lost to pink-white
Top band of lit batts burns to pale pink (median rgb 246/152/149); the cabinet reads as a lightbox, not tinted acrylic
Wall above the horn gets no colour from the speaker (median rgb 36/28/38, lum 30): the colour sits only in two side wedges
Horn is near black (lum 14, rgb 53/2/8) with a dark blob silhouette in it; reads as a dead dark slab above the glowing box
Plinth front reads mottled, like stained wood or rough concrete, rather than a clean black object (lum 11, r38 g3 b9 with blotchy texture)
Full-width dark grainy floor band between the wall foot and the first tile joint, ending in a hard horizontal line at y about 1340 that reads as a seam between two materials
Upper wall is evenly dim with no falloff or event; top third of the frame is dead space
Frame edges near crush (lum 14.5) with cool moon tint; board-form detail barely legible at the sides

changes.problem: The speaker stands almost against the wall (about 85 mm from the panels' face), so its own body shadows the wall behind and above it and the colour lands only as two side wedges.

evidence.measured: wall above horn median rgb 36/28/38, lum 30, versus the side wedge [960,900,1100,1100] rgb 204/54/52, lum 85

change.setting: set.props.7 to set.props.19 position y, set.props.0 position y, set.props.1 position y
change.from: props 7-19 y 0.45 (face at 0.30); props.0 y 1.05; props.1 y -0.05
change.to: props 7-19 y 1.15 (face at 1.00); props.0 y 1.75; props.1 y 0.65; extend the paving set.props.2 so it still reaches the new wall foot (centre y -1.0, size [60, 4.8])

changes.expected: Light leaving both side panels overlaps on the wall behind the speaker, so the wedges join into a halo that rises behind and above the horn; the wall above the horn turns visibly red.

changes.problem: The uplight is strong enough to clip the ports and top batts to pink-white, so Ember red is lost exactly where the product is brightest.
changes.expected: Ports and batts hold red saturation: port lum near 190, g and b under 140; the side wedges drop about 30% and c1/c3 carry the wall.

changes.problem: The haze box stops at y 0.28 and is too thin to show any glow, so there is no coloured air around the speaker to tie it to the wall and fill the space above it.

evidence.measured: flat lum 30, range 12: no glow or gradient above the speaker

change.to: box y max 0.95 (to just in front of the moved wall), density 0.05, anisotropy 0.5

changes.expected: A soft red bloom of lit air around and above the cabinet that falls off upward, which reads as night air and works for every colour (Fog gives a pale bloom, Smoke a faint one).

changes.problem: The floor strip from the wall foot to the first tile joint reads as a dark, dry, grainy band with a hard horizontal edge, as if two materials meet.

evidence.measured: band lum 9.7 with no tile structure, then a joint at y about 1340; profile down x 1300 from y 1250 goes 20.8 then 11.2 with a hard step

change.to: wet 0.55 uniform to the wall foot, puddle_m 0.8, puddle_edge 0.4, with a tile joint at the wall foot so the first visible joint is not a full-width seam

changes.expected: Tiles run continuously from wall to camera, with broken wet patches instead of a mirror strip and a dry band; the speaker's reflection stays.

changes.problem: The plinth's front face reads as a mottled stained-wood or concrete block, not a precise black object, so the speaker seems to stand on rubble.

evidence.measured: lum 11, r38 g3 b9, blotchy reflected texture visible at 3x crop

change.to: roughness 0.75 (bead-blasted black), ease 0.004 for a crisp edge that picks up a thin red line

changes.expected: The plinth reads as a solid matte black block with a fine lit top edge; no mottled reflection on its face.

changes.problem: The board-form at the frame's edges sinks toward black, so the set reads as a void at the sides rather than a wall at night.

change.to: 0.7 at [6.0, -2.0, 7.5], grazing the wall from the right so the boards and tie holes rake

changes.expected: Board lines legible at the edges at lum about 20, still clearly night, with the cool moon keeping the red as the only warm colour.

out_of_scope.request: Let the horn carry the speaker's colour (it is a black slab with a dark blob, lum 14)
out_of_scope.why: The horn's shape, its posts and the batts that stop light reaching it are fixed; only bounce from a coloured wall (c1, c3) can lift it in the frame.

out_of_scope.request: Move the uplight or add a rim of white light outside the cabinet footprint to paint more wall
out_of_scope.why: The lamp's place under the speaker is fixed, and white light outside the cabinet would wash the wall with white, not the product's colour.
